Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

WithinHostExperiment 0.99.3

Corrections

  • annotateCodonChange() and pNpSWithinHost() given CDS ranges no longer pass on txdbmaker’s warning that the TxDb they build has no genome assembly. txdbmaker 1.9.2 reworded that warning, which the package matched by its exact text, so two tests failed on the Bioconductor build machine. Both that warning and GenomicRanges’ out-of-bound warning are now recognised at any console width.

WithinHostExperiment 0.99.2

Corrections to functions that the earlier reviews had not examined. Each has a test that fails on 0.99.1. Several change results; each entry says what the function did and what it does now.

Interface changes

  • detectEmergingVariants() returns one more column, qc_from: whether a call at the earlier timepoint of the interval passed QC.
  • combineRows() and combineCols() are an error when the objects do not hold the same samples, or the same sites (see Corrections).
  • trackFrequency(), detectEmergingVariants() and plotFrequencyTrajectory() stop on a timepoint column of text that has no time order, such as "day10", as flagTemporalInconsistency() already did, and leave out samples without a timepoint, with a warning.
  • DESCRIPTION and _pkgdown.yml no longer give https://cuiweig.github.io/WithinHostExperiment/, which does not resolve; the repository address remains.

Corrections

  • A qcPass of NA counts as not passed wherever an analysis uses only passing calls. Ten masks wrote freq[!qc] <- NA, which R skips at an NA index, so such a call was used as passing by calcDiversity(), compareDiversity(), buildSFS(), calcNeutralityTests(), pNpSWithinHost(), exportPairFrequencies(), calcSharedVariants(), the bottleneck inputs, detectCrossContamination(), trackFrequency(), detectEmergingVariants(), plotFrequencyTrajectory() and plotFrequencySpectrum(). No package function writes NA into qcPass; one set by hand now counts as failed, as it already did in flagTemporalInconsistency() and the consensus.
  • A recorded frequency of 0, which a generic table holds for a site assessed without the allele, is no longer counted as a call. benchmarkCallers() and calcCallerConcordance() counted it as a called site, so a caller with two such rows scored precision 0.6 instead of 1. qcSummary() counted it in total_sites, as flagged once flagISNV() had run, and in median_freq: four calls among ten assessed sites gave a pass rate of 0.4 and a median frequency of 0. Every column of qcSummary() now describes the calls, median_depth included, and the help page defines each one. plotFrequencySpectrum() and panels a and d of plotQCDashboard() drew and counted it as an iSNV; panel a now leaves out a sample with no call, so a sample of recorded zeros does not stop the plot.
  • The percentage tick labels of plotFrequencySpectrum(), plotQCDashboard() and plotPairScatter() are rounded, where as.integer(x * 100) truncated them: a break at 4% could read 3, and one at 2.5% read 2.
  • trackFrequency(), detectEmergingVariants() and plotFrequencyTrajectory() read the timepoint column in time order, as flagTemporalInconsistency() does. Numbers given as text were sorted as text, so “1”, “2”, “10” gave an interval from 10 to 2, and an NA timepoint was sorted last and formed an interval ending in NA, with no warning.
  • trackFrequency() reports each call’s QC state in qc_passed. It read qcPass only with usePassedOnly = TRUE, which then removed the failing calls, so the column was TRUE on every row.
  • detectEmergingVariants() combines replicate samples taken at one timepoint by the mean of their calls before it forms intervals. Two replicates formed an interval from a timepoint to itself, a gap between them was reported as emergence, and the answer depended on the order of the columns.
  • detectEmergingVariants() forms intervals on every call and applies QC to their end points. It removed the calls that failed QC first, so after the default flagISNV() a start below minFreq (0.03), a recorded 0 included, could never be reported, and a timepoint that failed QC was skipped, joining the timepoints either side of it. The later point must now have a call that passed QC; the earlier point uses its passing calls, or all its calls when none passed, since a frequency below minFreq is the low start that emergence is measured from, and qc_from says which.
  • detectCrossContamination() keeps a source call that QC failed for its frequency alone. After the default flagISNV(), whose maxFreq is 0.5, every source above 50% was removed, the 80% source of the help page’s own example included. A failed source call above the strictest maxFreq of the filters applied is now used when it has the depth, alternative reads and strand balance that each of them asks for.
  • correctSFSBias() rounds the corrected spectrum as a total and shares its sites out among the bins by largest remainder. Rounding each bin left every bin of 7 or fewer iSNVs unchanged in a folded spectrum at threshold 0.03, and every bin of 16 or fewer in an unfolded one, so the truncation correction of the help page’s example spectrum kept its 15 sites while corrected became TRUE; it now gives 16, and nSites is the corrected total. The binomial method, which the example runs, still gives 15: at its median depth of 1,600 reads every bin is detectable.
  • combineRows() matches samples by column name, and combineCols() matches sites by sequence name, position, ref and alt. Both bound by position, so an object holding the same samples or sites in another order had its values written to the wrong ones without a message, and one holding others was relabelled. The same samples or sites in another order are now put in the first object’s order; others are an error that names the argument and what differs.
  • exactBottleneck(method = "exact_bb") derives a missing recipient alternative count at a known depth as round(altFreq * totalDepth), as readWithinHostTable(format = "generic") does. It took the count as 0, so an iVar table without its ALT_DP column made every recipient call an absence: on the shipped pair without the recipient’s counts it gave Nb 5 [3, 7] where the counts give 95 [21, 272]. A recipient with no frequency there still counts as 0 reads.

Documentation

  • The vignette describes the new behaviour of qcSummary(), correctSFSBias(), trackFrequency() and detectEmergingVariants(); the truncation correction of its donor spectrum gives 15 variants rather than 14.

WithinHostExperiment 0.99.1

Changes made in response to the Bioconductor review. The package has not been released, so functions are removed and renamed without a deprecation cycle, and objects saved with 0.99.0 must be rebuilt: an ISNVFilter saved then has a logical replicateConc, and a WithinHostSFS lacks the polarization and maxFreq slots. The WithinHostExperiment validity checks every filter in qcFilters, so validObject(), subsetting and combining report a filter saved with 0.99.0, with a message to rebuild it with ISNVFilter(), and flagISNV() given one names its replicateConc slot.

Interface changes

  • annotateFromGFF() is removed, together with the package’s own GFF3 and FASTA readers. annotateGenes(x, genes) labels each site with the gene it falls in, adding a GENE column to mcols(rowRanges(x)). genes is a GRanges, such as a GFF3 or GTF file read with rtracklayer::import(), or a TxDb, from which GenomicFeatures::genes() takes the ranges; the overlap is GenomicRanges::findOverlaps(). nameCol selects the label column, and an unknown one is an error that lists those available; collapse keeps the longest overlapping gene or all of them. When the sites and the genes share no sequence name the function stops and prints both sets, so a RefSeq/GenBank naming mismatch can no longer return a column of NA.
  • annotateCodonChange() is an S4 generic, annotateCodonChange(x, cds, ref), taking the coding sequences as a GRanges of CDS records, a GRangesList or a TxDb, and the reference as a DNAStringSet; a file path for either is refused with a message naming the Bioconductor reader to use. The consequence is computed by VariantAnnotation::predictCoding(), and the output columns take its names: TXNAME, GENEID, CONSEQUENCE, CDSLOC, PROTEINLOC, REFCODON, VARCODON, REFAA and VARAA replace GFF_FEATURE, REF_CODON, ALT_CODON, REF_AA, ALT_AA and AA_CLASS. A site in several overlapping coding sequences is resolved by collapse, the longest transcript by default; a nucleotide that one transcript reads twice, at a -1 ribosomal frameshift, keeps its first reading, and a message says so. Three classifications change with the delegation: losing a stop codon is nonsynonymous rather than nonsense, an alternative start codon (CTG or TTG) at the first base of a coding sequence reads as M, and a site whose reference codon holds an ambiguous base is left unannotated, with a warning. The reference length is recorded in seqlengths(rowRanges(x)). The GRanges and GRangesList routes build the TxDb with txdbmaker; a TxDb built with txdbmaker::makeTxDbFromGFF() can lack transcripts the GFF3 holds (for NC_045512.2 it drops the ORF1ab gene, so sites in ORF1a and ORF1ab are left unannotated), so the man page advises passing the CDS records instead.
  • dndsWithinHost() is replaced by pNpSWithinHost(x, cds, ref), which takes the same inputs as annotateCodonChange() and calls it for the reference and variant codon of each iSNV. The quantity is a ratio of nonsynonymous to synonymous polymorphism within a host, not of substitutions between sequences, so the Jukes-Cantor correction is no longer applied. Nei-Gojobori sites are counted over the distinct codons of the genome, so codons shared by same-frame overlapping coding sequences, such as ORF1a and ORF1ab, are counted once, and a warning names the overlapping transcripts. Per gene, a shared codon counts in each gene that reads it, and so does an iSNV in it, each by that gene’s own transcript. On the README’s SARS-CoV-2 call set the pooled ratio moves from 0.2857 to 0.2867 with the correction removed. The man page says why the sites are counted here rather than by MSA2dist: MSA2dist::codonmat2pnps() and dnastring2kaks() compare aligned sequence pairs and cannot take per-site calls; for each of the 61 sense codons the sites equal those of codonmat2pnps(), which a test checks.
  • consensusSequences(x, ref, minFreq = 0.5) is new. It writes each sample’s substitutions at or above minFreq into the reference and returns one sequence per sample as a DNAStringSet; insertions and deletions are not applied, so the sequences stay aligned to the reference and to one another. region returns one coding sequence, joined across its parts and read in its own direction. dN/dS between hosts can then be estimated with MSA2dist::dnastring2kaks(), which is suggested, rather than with a model of this package’s own. When ref and the sites share no sequence name it stops and names both sets, and a region on a sequence missing from ref is reported as such.
  • readWithinHost() keeps its arguments but reads files with VariantAnnotation::readVcf() instead of parsing VCF text, and splits records with several alternative alleles with expand(). A per-allele field that the header does not declare Number=A on such a record stops the import, since readVcf() would give every allele the first allele’s value; a field declared Number=R, whose first value is the reference allele’s, stops it on any file, where that value was read as the alternative allele’s count or frequency. genome takes a DNAStringSet, not a file path; its lengths, or those of ##contig header lines, are recorded in seqlengths() for every sequence named, with a call or without. A genome that names none of the sequences the calls lie on, or is shorter than a called position, is an error, since every per-site statistic would divide by its length. A file holding more than one sample is refused; as(vcf, "WithinHostExperiment") converts a VCF object with all of its samples. Coercion to and from VRanges keeps every recorded sequence and its length, so the genome length survives a round trip, and a sequence name may contain ‘:’, which it used to be split on.
  • calcDiversity() and compareDiversity() lose the genomeLength argument. The length that pi and watterson divide by is read from seqlengths(rowRanges(x)), summed over every sequence recorded for the reference, so that a segment of a segmented genome without calls still counts, and a length that is not recorded is an error saying how to record it. calcDiversity() gains n_sites_assessed, the sites at which a sample has any call before QC, and detection_limit, the strictest minFreq of the filters applied, so that a diversity of zero after QC can be told apart from a sample with no calls. example_whe records its 1000-base segment length; its values are unchanged.
  • calcNeutralityTests() loses the genomeLength argument it required. Tajima’s D and Fu’s Fs use the nucleotide diversity summed over the genome, which the frequencies give directly, so the length was divided in and multiplied back out and changed no output beyond rounding error; passing it is now an error.
  • validateDiversity() is renamed checkDiversityPlausibility(). Its ranges are the package’s own heuristics, not literature values, and the man page lists every one. Every sample of a calcDiversity() table is checked, where only the first row was checked before, and the result names the sample; a missing value is reported as not in range.
  • ISNVFilter() loses the minBaseQual and minMapQual slots and arguments: the object holds no per-site quality, so they could be recorded but never applied, and quality filtering belongs in the variant caller.
  • replicateConc holds a ConcordanceRule, or NULL for none, where it held a logical that was recorded but never applied. ConcordanceRule(freqTolerance, requireBothDetected) takes the two settings of flagReplicateDiscordance(), and flagISNV() applies it after the per-sample thresholds, flagging what that function flags and recording the same two qcLog rows, so the rule is stored with the other thresholds in qcFilters. A rule with no replicate_group of two or more samples to compare is an error; samples without a replicate are named in a warning. A logical replicateConc is refused, and so is a rule that would flag nothing: a freqTolerance of 1 or more with requireBothDetected = FALSE, since frequencies lie in [0, 1]. ConcordanceRule() refuses a factor, string or logical tolerance and a requireBothDetected that is not TRUE or FALSE, rather than convert them, and flagReplicateDiscordance() now checks its arguments in the same way. flagISNV() checks its filter with validObject() first, so a threshold or rule changed with @<- into a value its class refuses is an error rather than a step applied.
  • consensusISNV() keeps the seqinfo() of its inputs, merged, and stops when a sequence’s length, circularity or genome differs between them. It takes each sample’s colData row from the first input that holds the sample, and keeps a column for every input sample, NA where no site passed, with a warning naming any sample that fewer than min_callers inputs hold, since such a sample cannot reach consensus. Sequence lengths, host, role and pair columns used to be dropped, so calcDiversity() stopped for want of a genome length and the transmission functions found no pairs.
  • The results of quickBottleneck() and exactBottleneck() gain n_excluded, the donor variants at or above threshold left out of the estimate, by reason (see below).

Statistical safeguards

  • WithinHostSFS gains a polarization slot: "none" for a folded spectrum, "reference" for an unfolded spectrum of alternative-allele frequencies, which treats the reference allele as ancestral, or "outgroup". Validity ties it to folded, and show() prints it and labels the stored depth a median, which it is.
  • neutralityFromSFS() stops on a folded spectrum, where it printed a note and returned a value, because Fay and Wu’s H needs derived-allele frequencies; its result records the polarisation it used. It also stops on a spectrum without a genome length, where it returned values summed over the genome under the label “per site”. buildSFS() now takes that length from seqlengths(rowRanges(whe)) when it is not given, as calcDiversity() does.
  • WithinHostSFS gains a maxFreq slot, the highest frequency a call could keep through QC. buildSFS() sets it to the smallest maxFreq among the filters applied with flagISNV() when it uses QC-passed calls, and to 1 otherwise. neutralityFromSFS() stops on an unfolded spectrum whose cap is below 1: the default ISNVFilter() removes every call above 0.5, which empties the classes Fay and Wu’s H weights most, so H could not reveal an excess of high-frequency variants whatever the data. The spectrum must be built from the unfiltered object flagged with maxFreq = 1. show() prints the cap when it is below 1.
  • neutralityFromSFS() computes pi and theta_H on the same derived-allele classes, round(mid * n) held within 1 to n - 1, with Fay and Wu’s normalisation. Before, pi came from unrounded midpoints without the n/(n-1) factor, which biased H by about -theta/n under neutrality even on a complete spectrum. H is now centred on 0 only when every class from 1 to n - 1 is observed and each bin holds one class; the detection threshold and wide bins still shift it, to about -0.03 theta on the expected neutral spectrum under the defaults (20 bins, threshold 0.03, n = 100), much as before. pi, Tajima’s D, Fu’s Fs and H from this function change.
  • compareSFS() stops unless both spectra share their bin breaks, their folding, their polarisation and their QC frequency cap, and neither is bias-corrected; it used to compare any two spectra with the same number of bins. A spectrum from before QC can therefore be compared with one from after it only when the filters kept maxFreq = 1. When either spectrum is empty it runs no test and returns NA diagnostics, where it returned NaN on a positive df.
  • A site counts as segregating only when its frequency after QC lies strictly between 0 and 1. This applies to n_sites, S and theta_pi in calcNeutralityTests(), to richness, watterson and chao1 in calcDiversity(), and to the sites buildSFS() bins. A frequency of 0, or of 1, a fixed difference that iVar reports, used to be counted without adding to pi, which pulled Tajima’s D down.
  • tajimaD() returns NA, with a warning, below three segregating sites, where it returned 0 at none and a number at one or two, and when the sample size rounds below four, where the variance of D is zero and it returned Inf or NaN. fusFs() returns NA, with a warning, when there is no segregating site or theta_pi is 0, where it returned 0, a number where none is defined; above n = 500 it computes the Ewens tail exactly, where a normal approximation made the value jump at the switch. calcNeutralityTests() reports n_sites, the number of sites each statistic rests on, documents every rule under which D or Fs is NA and warns once per cause. A sample with no calls gives zero diversity and zero segregating sites rather than an uninformative error, in calcNeutralityTests() and in calcDiversity().
  • The help pages of fusFs(), calcNeutralityTests() and neutralityFromSFS() say that the haplotype count is set to S + 1, the infinite-sites maximum. The value therefore carries no haplotype information and is pushed below 0 under neutrality, increasingly so as theta grows (-7.00 at theta = 5 with n = 100, -0.37 at theta = 1), so a negative Fs is not evidence of expansion.
  • pNpSWithinHost() counts an iSNV only through a reading whose codon carries sites. A reading in a stop codon, including the loss of a stop codon, is not counted, since a stop codon carries no sites; where coding sequences overlap, such an iSNV is counted through a transcript that reads it in a sense codon, and one that every transcript reads in a stop codon enters neither n_S nor n_N. Each call is classified by translating its reference and variant codons with the standard genetic code and no initiator rule, so ATG to CTG or TTG at the first base of a coding sequence is nonsynonymous here, as ATG carries no synonymous site, although annotateCodonChange() reports it as synonymous. The rule applies to the totals and to each gene’s counts. The vignette donor’s ratio moves from 1.11 (3 synonymous, 11 nonsynonymous) to 1.36 (2 and 9); the README figure values do not change.
  • calcSharedVariants() gains minDepth, by default the strictest minDepth applied with flagISNV() (100 when none was), and splits the donor-only count into n_donor_only_adequate_depth, n_donor_only_low_depth and n_donor_only_unknown_depth, with n_donor_only_recipient_failed_qc for the sites where the recipient made a call that QC removed, which are not absences; only the first is evidence that a variant was lost in transmission. n_donor_only is still their sum.
  • exportPairFrequencies() and calcSharedVariants() take a host to carry an allele only where its frequency is known and above 0. A site that a table read with readWithinHostTable(format = "generic") lists with aaf = 0 counted as shared when no QC had been applied; it is now an absence, split by the recipient’s depth. recipient_freq keeps the recorded 0, and sites that neither host carries are no longer listed; a pair with no such site gives an empty table.
  • asViralBottleneckInput(), quickBottleneck() and every method of exactBottleneck() leave out, with a message, a donor variant at a site where QC removed a recipient call at or above threshold. Such a call, for example one above maxFreq where the variant rose towards fixation, was written as a frequency of 0 and scored as a variant lost in transmission, while exact_bb used its raw read counts. A removed call below threshold is an absence by the estimators’ own definition and is still written as 0, and a recorded 0 is never taken for a call.
  • exactBottleneck(method = "exact_bb") leaves out, with a message, donor variants whose recipient depth is unknown, which includes every site the recipient’s VCF file does not list. They added the same constant to the log-likelihood at every Nb, so the estimate and the likelihood-ratio interval do not change, but n_variants counted them as used and a bootstrap interval resampled them; they are now counted in n_excluded, and the manual page says that exact_bb then sees no loss in transmission.
  • The estimators that work from frequencies, quickBottleneck() and the presence_absence and wright_fisher methods of exactBottleneck(), use donor variants from threshold to 1 - threshold, as the published methods do. A donor variant at frequency 1 that the recipient lacked gave a log-likelihood of -Inf at every Nb and an estimate of 1 without a warning. Both functions now stop when the log-likelihood is not finite at any Nb of the grid.
  • quickBottleneck() checks maxNb, where maxNb = 0 returned an estimate of length 0 with two base-R warnings. It and exactBottleneck() refuse a maxNb that is not a single whole number from 1 to the integer limit; exactBottleneck() truncated 2.5 to 2 and accepted text and logical values. Both refuse a threshold that is not a single number above 0 and below 0.5: at 0 every recipient frequency counts as present, and from 0.5 no donor variant lies between threshold and 1 - threshold. quickBottleneck() did not check it, and exactBottleneck() accepted any value from 0 to 1.
  • flagReplicateDiscordance(), and the replicate step of flagISNV(), let a frequency difference equal to freqTolerance pass, as documented. A decimal subtraction such as 0.20 - 0.15 rounds to just above 0.05, so 39 of the 96 two-decimal pairs 0.05 apart were flagged; the comparison now allows for rounding error, and so does the frequency spread of consensusISNV(). The vignette’s counts are unchanged. The replicate step also counts the cells it flags when qcPass holds NA, where the qcLog recorded n_flagged as NA.
  • flagTemporalInconsistency() counts the distinct timepoints at which a site is detected within a host, not the samples, so technical replicates taken at one timepoint no longer make a variant persistent; minConsecutive runs over those timepoints, and a host sampled at a single timepoint is not classified. Timepoints may be numbers, dates, date-times, time differences, a factor in time order, or text that reads as numbers; other text is an error, and a blank is a missing timepoint. A qcPass cell that is NA counts as not passed, where an NA cell with a frequency stopped the function with an uninformative error, and is left NA when the site is flagged. Samples with no timepoint are not counted, with a warning.
  • flagStrandBiasSCI() computes each sample’s global strand ratio over the sites that sample called. The ratio was summed without removing missing values, so in a multi-sample object any sample with an absent call scored NA throughout and nothing in it was flagged. sciStrandBias() scores NA at a site with a missing count and leaves it out of the sums, and it refuses negative, infinite and non-numeric counts, where a negative count returned -Inf.
  • buildSFS() checks sampleIdx, nBins, threshold and fold and names the one at fault; two samples are no longer pooled, and a filter with a maxFreq of 0, which leaves no call to count, is an error giving that value. It folds a sample with no passing call to an empty spectrum, where it failed and took buildSFSList() down with it. piISNV(), shannonISNV() and simpsonISNV() stop on text and on frequencies outside [0, 1], where piISNV() returned a negative diversity.
  • flagPrimerSites() stops, naming both sets, when the primers and the sites share no sequence name, where it reported that no site overlapped a primer and flagged nothing.
  • exactBottleneck(method = "wright_fisher") says in a message that its result is a heuristic score, not a likelihood; exact_bb and presence_absence are the estimators.

Corrections

  • readWithinHostTable() reads the sequence and allele columns as text. read.delim() and read.csv() turned a column that held only “T” into the logical TRUE, so an iVar table whose calls were all C>T was imported with the allele TRUE.
  • consensusISNV() counts each caller once per site and sample: a caller that listed the same site and allele twice supplied two of the min_callers votes and was named twice in caller_names. It no longer splits a sequence name at its colons, which put every site on a contig such as HLA-A*01:01 at one wrong position.
  • detectCrossContamination() stops, listing the available columns, when runCol is not a single column of colData; a misspelt name used to compare every sample with every other without a word. Samples whose run is NA are left out with a warning giving their number.
  • plotPairScatter() draws a donor variant whose recipient frequency is a recorded 0 as donor-only, where it drew it as shared, and says there is nothing to plot for a pair in which neither host carries an allele.

Performance

  • consensusISNV() builds one table of calls instead of looping over every cell: 3,000 sites in 20 samples from two callers took about four and a half minutes and take half a second, with the same result.
  • detectEmergingVariants() orders the trajectories once and compares each timepoint with the next in one step, giving the same rows in the same order: 3,000 sites in 20 samples took about a minute and take a fraction of a second. Samples with no host are left out with a warning, where they stopped the function.

Dependencies

  • Biostrings and GenomicFeatures are imported; BiocStyle, rtracklayer, txdbmaker and MSA2dist are suggested. rtracklayer is not imported.
  • graphics and tools, which the package already used, are declared in Imports; covr, which nothing used, is no longer suggested.
  • LongRead is removed from biocViews.

Documentation

  • The vignette is rewritten as teaching material with BiocStyle: each code chunk is introduced by what it does and followed by how to read its output, terms are defined where they are introduced and collected in a glossary, the qcLog and qcFilters slots that WithinHostExperiment adds to RangedSummarizedExperiment are described one by one, and installation is from Bioconductor only.
  • The man pages of readWithinHost() and readWithinHostTable() list what the import does not read. The FILTER column of a VCF and iVar’s PASS column are not read, so records the caller rejected are imported as calls; per-strand counts are not read, so the strand-bias step of flagISNV() does not run on an imported object; and insertions and deletions are imported as width-1 rows in the caller’s notation, without being told apart from substitutions. Each page shows how to drop rejected records, or keep substitutions only, before QC.
  • The WithinHostExperiment class page states that assays must be ordinary R matrices, and a qcPass assay held as a DelayedArray or another backend is refused with a message saying so.
  • The README marks installation from GitHub as not recommended and states the source and terms of use of the four Bendall et al. (2023) excerpts that ship in inst/extdata.
  • The pkgdown reference index gives every topic a section with a one-line description, in place of a catch-all.
  • inst/scripts/make_extdata.R, which ships, records how each file in inst/extdata was made and with which seed.
  • readme_figure_output/ is removed from the repository root. The values and checksums the README is checked against are kept in inst/scripts/readme_values/, and inst/scripts/reproduce_all.R rebuilds every derived file from the raw data and checks it against the committed copy.

Tests

  • tests/testthat/test-corrections.R holds a regression test for each item of ‘Corrections made before submission’ under 0.99.0 that still applies, named after the bug it guards against, and the README’s statement that QC cannot raise pi as a test. The removed codon annotator is kept in tests/testthat/helper-reference-codon.R as a reference implementation, and annotateCodonChange() is tested against it.
  • Each behavioural change listed above has a regression test, and most test names say what the behaviour used to be. The replicate rule of flagISNV() is tested at a tolerance other than the default, with requireBothDetected = FALSE, on calls that fail a threshold, at the tolerance boundary from both sides and on a group of three replicates, with hard-coded expected flags.

WithinHostExperiment 0.99.0

Corrections made before submission

Before submission every exported function was read against its documentation and run on fixtures built to break it, and each discrepancy found was fixed, documented as implemented, or both. The items below record what changed. In 0.99.1 each item that still applies was pinned by a regression test in tests/testthat/test-corrections.R, named after the bug it guards against (for example exact_bb matches sites by chrom, pos and allele (was: pos only)), so that none can return unnoticed.

  • compareSFS() suppressed every warning from chisq.test(), so a p-value resting on expected counts below 5 looked as trustworthy as any other. It now returns the smallest expected count and chisq_approx_ok, which is FALSE in that case, and silences only that one warning; the statistic and p-value are unchanged.
  • flagTemporalInconsistency() classified each site with the last host processed and flagged transient sites in every sample. Sites are now classified within each host and flagged only in the samples of hosts where they are transient.
  • exactBottleneck(method = "exact_bb") matched donor variants to rows by position alone, which is wrong for segmented genomes, and paired donor frequencies with recipient read counts by index when some sites did not match. Sites are now matched by chromosome, position and allele. An estimate that reaches maxNb triggers a warning.
  • The documentation of exactBottleneck() states how exact_bb departs from Sobel Leonard et al. (2017) and that wright_fisher is a heuristic score.
  • flagISNV(), calcDiversity() and calcNeutralityTests() stop on arguments they do not use.
  • adaptiveFilter("ont") uses minDepth = 60, the depth above which Bull et al. (2020) found over 99% sensitivity and precision for single-nucleotide variants; it was 30.
  • correctSFSBias(), compareSFS(), the WithinHostSFS bins and depth slot, consensusISNV(), flagReplicateDiscordance() and validateDiversity() are documented as implemented: truncation rescales the whole spectrum, bins are right-closed, the stored depth is a median, the consensus object holds only allele frequencies, and the diversity ranges are heuristic plausibility bounds rather than literature values.
  • ISNVFilter() documents minBaseQual, minMapQual and replicateConc as recorded but not applied, and flagISNV() warns when they are set, instead of ignoring them silently. WithinHostExperiment() requires an altFreq assay, as documented.
  • trackFrequency() builds its table in one vectorised step, which is much faster on genome-wide data and gives the same rows.
  • plotFrequencySpectrum(), plotPairScatter() and plotQCDashboard() clip the view with coordinate limits instead of removing data outside the axis range, which dropped jittered points with a warning; plotFrequencyTrajectory() uses the Okabe-Ito palette, as described, and plotSFS() recycles it for more than eight samples.

New features

  • WithinHostExperiment S4 class extending RangedSummarizedExperiment for within-host pathogen iSNV data, with setValidity enforcing structural invariants.
  • Multi-caller import: readWithinHost() reads VCFs in the LoFreq, Freebayes, generic and iVar-style field layouts with auto-detection (ivar variants writes a TSV, so an iVar-style VCF comes from a converter). readWithinHostTable() handles the iVar TSV directly, and generic CSV.
  • Replicate-aware QC: flagISNV() applies configurable quality filters without removing data. flagReplicateDiscordance() identifies discordant technical replicates with full provenance logging. flagPrimerSites() masks amplicon primer regions.
  • Diversity indices: shannonISNV(), piISNV() (with optional finite-sample correction per Nei 1987), wattersonISNV(), simpsonISNV(), chao1ISNV(), and calcDiversity() for per-sample within-host diversity.
  • Neutrality tests: tajimaD(), fusFs(), and calcNeutralityTests() for site-frequency-spectrum-based neutrality testing with deep-sequencing-aware sample size capping.
  • Site frequency spectrum as a first-class object: WithinHostSFS S4 class stores the within-host SFS with metadata (sample, genome length, depth, detection threshold). buildSFS() / buildSFSList() construct from a WHE; correctSFSBias() applies ascertainment bias correction for the detection threshold (truncation or binomial method); neutralityFromSFS() computes Tajima’s D, Fu’s Fs, and Fay and Wu’s H (new) from a single SFS object; compareSFS() tests SFS homogeneity between samples; plotSFS() provides publication-quality SFS visualisation.
  • Temporal QC for longitudinal data: flagTemporalInconsistency() identifies transient iSNVs that appear at only one timepoint (likely artefacts) versus persistent ones detected across multiple consecutive timepoints. Supports configurable minTimepoints and minConsecutive thresholds.
  • Cross-contamination detection: detectCrossContamination() identifies index-hopping signatures where a high-frequency variant in one sample appears at suspiciously low frequency in a co-sequenced sample, consistent with adapter exchange during pooled sequencing. Returns a structured DataFrame of suspect events with source/sink frequencies and run metadata.
  • GFF3 annotation: annotateFromGFF() overlaps variant sites with gene models from a GFF3 file, adding GFF_FEATURE to mcols(rowRanges) for use with dndsWithinHost(). annotateCodonChange() extends this with CDS-aware codon translation: given a GFF3 and reference FASTA, it determines the affected codon, translates both reference and alternative alleles using the standard genetic code, and classifies each SNV as Synonymous, Nonsynonymous, or Nonsense. (0.99.1 replaces both with functions that take Bioconductor objects and delegates the consequence call to VariantAnnotation::predictCoding().)
  • Selection analysis: dndsWithinHost() estimates within-host dN/dS with the Nei-Gojobori counting method, normalising by the synonymous and nonsynonymous sites of the CDS features in a GFF3 and reference FASTA, with Jukes-Cantor correction; estimateSelectionCoefficient() for time-series selection coefficient inference.
  • Multi-caller consensus: consensusISNV() for deriving consensus variant calls across callers, calcCallerConcordance() for inter-caller agreement metrics, benchmarkCallers() for caller performance comparison.
  • Longitudinal analysis: trackFrequency() for tracking variant allele frequencies over time, detectEmergingVariants() for identifying newly arising variants, plotFrequencyTrajectory() for publication-quality trajectory plots.
  • Transmission analysis: transmissionPairs(), exportPairFrequencies(), calcSharedVariants(), and quickBottleneck() (approximate beta-binomial MLE, Sobel Leonard et al. 2017) for bottleneck estimation.
  • Exact bottleneck estimation: exactBottleneck() offers a beta-binomial likelihood over the transmitted virions that models finite recipient depth, in the spirit of Sobel Leonard et al. (2017) with two stated departures, a presence-absence likelihood, and a Wright-Fisher score, which is a heuristic rather than a likelihood.
  • Strand bias detection: sciStrandBias() and flagStrandBiasSCI() for strand bias filtering that accounts for unequal strand coverage.
  • Adaptive filtering: adaptiveFilter() for technology-specific QC presets (Illumina, ONT, PacBio HiFi).
  • Diversity modelling: fitDiversityModel() for regression modelling of diversity measures, multitestCorrection() for multiple testing correction, permutationTest() for non-parametric hypothesis testing.
  • Validation: validateDiversity() compares diversity estimates with wide heuristic plausibility ranges per pathogen, not with literature values.
  • ViralBottleneck bridge: asViralBottleneckInput() exports standardised data for the ViralBottleneck package (Zheng et al. 2025).
  • Interoperability: as(whe, "VRanges"), as(vr, "WithinHostExperiment"), and as(whe, "data.frame") for seamless integration.
  • Batch operations: methods for the S4Vectors combineRows() and combineCols() generics merge experiments together with their QC logs and filters.
  • Publication-quality visualisation: plotFrequencySpectrum(), plotPairScatter(), plotQCDashboard(), and plotFrequencyTrajectory() with a colour-blind-safe palette (Wong 2011).
  • SARS-CoV-2 case study in the vignette, with the same workflow run on synthetic examples for influenza A, HIV-1 and M. tuberculosis.
